name: Halfburn Graphic Tee — Faded Bloc Print
description: Boxy, slightly oversized tee in washed-out terracotta with a cracked bloc-print graphic across the chest — geometric shapes that might be a skyline, might be abstract, hard to tell anymore. Fabric is mid-weight synth-cotton, pre-softened. Looks like it's been worn a hundred times even when new.
functionality: Breathable enough for humid summers; holds shape after repeated washing.
what_it_says: You're relaxed, maybe a little nostalgic, definitely not trying to impress anyone.
manufacturer: Halfburn Studio — independent screen print shop, Circuit District
story_hooks: The geometric print is actually a coded map — someone at Halfburn Studio hid something in the design.
This colorway was discontinued after a corponation flagged the bloc imagery as resembling their proprietary logo.

physical_description.visual_profile: Relaxed, lived-in streetwear staple with a deliberately faded, distressed aesthetic. The boxy cut sits loose on the frame with a slightly dropped shoulder line. The chest graphic dominates—a cracked, weathered bloc print in competing geometric shapes that read as both architectural and abstract, suggesting either a fragmented skyline or pure compositional noise. Overall impression is deliberately worn despite being new.
physical_description.fit: Boxy and slightly oversized with a straight cut through the torso and sleeves. Sits relaxed at the shoulders without structure. Length falls to mid-hip with minimal tapering. The cut suggests comfort over silhouette—typical of Tier 3 casual wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Mid-weight synth-cotton blend, pre-softened and treated for a worn, supple hand-feel. Durable enough for frequent washing and extended wear.
physical_description.texture: Soft with a slightly napped surface from pre-treatment. The bloc-print graphic has visible cracking and ink fade across the surface, revealing white base fabric beneath. Areas show controlled distressing as if handled and washed extensively.
physical_description.color_scheme: Washed-out terracotta base with faded charcoal and deep grey bloc-print graphic. The cracking exposes ivory and pale cream undertones, creating a three-tone effect. The overall palette reads as sun-bleached and time-worn.
physical_description.closures: None—simple crew neck pullover with no visible fasteners or hardware.
distinctive_features: Deliberately cracked bloc-print graphic suggesting age and wear
Ambiguous geometric design—readable as skyline or pure abstraction
Intentional fading that makes new garment appear vintage
Hand-screen printed quality with slight ink variation
Halfburn Studio branding (assumed on back neck or sleeve)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional streetwear with Tier 5 aesthetic appeal. Affordable independent production, not corpo mass-market.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals sub-grade or working-class street culture with appreciation for independent design. Worn by those who value authenticity over pristine condition—artists, mechanics, transit workers, off-grid communities. Deliberately anti-corporate despite being new.
physical_description.condition_typical: Appears aged and worn from the moment of purchase. Continues to break in and soften with actual wear. The graphic will continue to crack and fade naturally, making each garment unique over time.
